title: Active-Active
subtitle: Multi-master request serving, concurrent write conflict resolution (LWW, CRDTs), and instant zero-downtime failover.
keyTakeaways: In an Active-Active topology, all deployed regions simultaneously accept both read and write traffic, providing near-zero RTO and continuous verification that every region's stack is hot and functional.

Accepting concurrent writes to the same entity in multiple regions without synchronous coordination inevitably creates write-write conflicts that must be resolved via Last-Write-Wins (LWW), CRDTs, or application merge logic.
Distributed state machines (such as rate limiters, idempotency keys, and session stores) must be designed for eventual convergence when operating across active-active clusters.

sections.heading: Multi-Master Write Conflicts & Convergence Models
sections.body: When two regions both accept writes without a global lock, concurrent modifications to the same record within the replication window (~50-200ms) produce divergent state. An Active-Active architecture is only as sound as its conflict resolution strategy.
bullets: Last-Write-Wins (LWW): Each write carries a timestamp (physical NTP or Hybrid Logical Clock). The highest timestamp overwrites the other. Simple, but silently drops concurrent updates (e.g., two devices adding different items to a cart) and is vulnerable to clock skew.

Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs): Data structures (PN-Counters, LWW-Element-Set, OR-Set) where concurrent mutations commute, associate, and are idempotent, mathematically guaranteeing convergence without coordination.

Single-Writer Affinity (Partitioned Active-Active): Both regions are active overall, but any individual entity (`user_id` or `order_id`) has a designated primary write region, routing rare cross-region writes over the WAN.

sections.heading: Traffic Evacuation & Capacity Headroom in Active-Active
sections.body: A major advantage of Active-Active over Active-Passive is eliminating 'failover fear': because every region serves live production traffic 24/7, caches, connection pools, and JIT compilers are always warm.
bullets: Anycast / BGP & DNS Traffic Shifting: Global edge networks (Cloudflare, AWS Global Accelerator) monitor regional health endpoints and withdraw unhealthy regional routes within seconds without waiting for client DNS TTL expiration.

The N+1 Regional Headroom Rule: If running 2 Active-Active regions, neither region can exceed 50% capacity (ideally 40%) during peak hours; otherwise, failing over one region into the other triggers a cascading overload outage.

Replication Loop Prevention: Cross-region CDC/Kafka MirrorMaker pipelines must tag replicated events with an `origin_region` header so the receiving region does not re-publish the event back to the source region in an infinite loop.

tradeOffs.pros: Lowest write latency everywhere; any region can absorb any user's traffic instantly without WAN forwarding.
tradeOffs.cons: Complex conflict resolution (CRDTs/LWW); no strict read-after-write consistency across regions; hard to enforce unique constraints.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Shopping carts, media playback state, social likes/views, DNS, and collaborative document editing.

tradeOffs.pros: Strong single-region ACID transactional guarantees per user while keeping all regions actively serving traffic.
tradeOffs.cons: Failover of a region requires flipping shard ownership and tolerating a brief RPO window of un-replicated async writes.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Multi-tenant B2B SaaS, banking accounts, and order management systems.

interviewTip: When proposing Active-Active in an interview, immediately ask: 'Are writes commutative, or do we have strict uniqueness/balance constraints?' If strict constraints exist (like preventing double-spending a wallet), use User-Sharded Active-Active rather than Last-Write-Wins.
